free_tier.stated: A free plan is claimed at 66 credits a day, and it is not confirmable from the vendor: three routes to the price list failed on 2026-10-22. Third-party accounts conflict. One review states 'The free plan gives all logged-in users 66 daily credits that expire after 24 hours' with a 5-second 720p clip at 30 credits. Another, dated 2026-09-26, states the opposite: 'the 66 free credits a day figure repeated across the web does not appear on any official Kling page we checked' and quotes Kling's own credits policy as granting daily credits to 'subscribers ... during the event (as shown in the interface)'.

interface_detail: inferred from the tooling the provider documents; not probed
chaining: no chain can be proposed on an unverified allowance. Where the 66-a-day claim holds, two five-second clips a day is a slow storyboard feed; where it does not, is paid-only and Runway's 125-credit trial recorded in this file is the comparable entry.

limits.value: if the 66-a-day allowance exists it is capped by resolution and watermark rather than by volume: the free tier is reported at 360p to 540p with a forced watermark and no commercial rights, so two clips a day at 30 credits each is the whole budget.
